title: Knox Baird et al. v. Grace Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaints sustained on Issues 1–2 and 4; sustained in part on Issue 3, with the overbroad document directive vacated; denied on Issue 5; sustained on Issue 6, with the trial stay annulled; Issue 7 was not reached. Session trials were to proceed.
first_summary: Session elders challenged Presbytery’s handling of a mediation complaint, its document and congregational-notice directives, its review of BCO 40-5 reports, and its stay of Session trials. The SJC sustained the complaints in the main, vacated the document directive, upheld appointment of a review committee, and annulled the stay because Presbytery had not first cited the Session.
summary: Session elders challenged Presbytery’s handling of a withdrawn mediation complaint, document and congregational-notice directives, BCO 40-5 reports, and a stay of Session trials. The SJC sustained the complaints in the main: the mediation complaint was never formally filed and became moot; Presbytery could require official record materials but not compel personal communications or force the Session to address its congregation; and the stay lacked a prior BCO 40-5 citation. It upheld appointing a committee to examine the reports, did not reach alleged partiality, vacated the overbroad directive, annulled the stay, and returned the trials to Session.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case Nos. 2023-06 and 2023-08 were jointly decided as Baird et al. v. Grace Presbytery; the SJC adopted the decision 17-0 (lines 9–17, 406).
evidence_notes.dispute: Seven issues challenged the Blue Hen complaint proceedings, information and notice directives, committee appointment, and trial stay (lines 139–157; printed pp. 795–796).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Issue-level judgments appear at lines 158–166; operative reasons and relief appear at lines 179–181, 214–324, and 326–404.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Official records could be required, but extra personal correspondence could only be requested, not compelled; use of communications obtained by a prosecutor was not decided. Partiality was not reached (lines 243–324, 396–404). The concurrence addressed unredacted language in a brief, not the merits (lines 423–446).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No external decision was incorporated by reference.
